summary: Frontend-only end-to-end test of the new JWT superadmin auth (login, session, change-password, logout, PDF token, regressions). 22/24 checks pass. One clear UX bug: entering a WRONG current password in the Change Password dialog logs the user out (redirect to /login) instead of showing pwd-error, because the axios 401 interceptor whitelists only /auth/login. All other flows pass: guard/redirect, bad-password error, correct login, user menu (email + change-password + logout items), lt_token persisted in localStorage, F5 session persistence, client-side validations (<8 chars, mismatch), successful change → toast → dialog closed, logout clears token, re-login with new password works, old password refused, ORIGINAL password RESTORED and final login with the original password verified OK. Vehicles page renders with images (0 broken/11), vehicle drawer opens, Timeline and Alertes pages load, and Rapport PDF is exported through window.open with ?token= (fetched status 200, no 401). No console 401s during normal navigation (the one 401 captured is the deliberate wrong-current-password test).

minor.issue: Returns 401 on wrong current_password. Combined with the frontend's global 401 interceptor this causes an unwanted logout. Either return 400/422 for wrong-current, or exclude /auth/change-password from the interceptor's redirect (frontend fix preferred).

ui_bugs.issue: Submitting the change-password form with a wrong CURRENT password triggers the axios 401 response interceptor in /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js (lines 16-25), which clears lt_token and redirects to /login. Expected behavior: keep the user logged in and display 'Mot de passe actuel incorrect' via pwd-error. Reproduce: log in, open user menu → 'Changer le mot de passe', enter wrong current password + valid new/confirm, click Enregistrer → user is silently logged out. Fix: whitelist '/auth/change-password' in the 401 interceptor exactly like '/auth/login' is whitelisted, so authChangePassword rejects into the dialog's setError branch.

action_items: In /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js, extend the 401 interceptor whitelist: skip the setToken(null)+redirect for URLs containing '/auth/change-password' (and ideally '/auth/me' too, since a token expiry mid-bootstrap is already handled by AuthContext catch). Concretely, change the guard to something like: const url = String(error?.config?.url || ''); if (error?.response?.status === 401 && !url.includes('/auth/login') && !url.includes('/auth/change-password')) { ... }
critical_code_review_comments: api.js 401 interceptor is too aggressive: it treats any 401 as a session-expiry logout, but /auth/change-password legitimately returns 401 on wrong current_password. Whitelist that route (and any other auth-verification route that can legitimately return 401 without meaning session-invalid).

AuthContext.logout() uses window.location.assign('/login') — fine, but the interceptor also does window.location.assign('/login') and clears the token. Consider centralizing logout in AuthContext so React state stays in sync (currently the interceptor mutates localStorage but does not call setUser(null) from context).
seed_data_creation: None. Password was temporarily rotated to 'TempAgent-2026!' during the change-password flow and RESTORED to the original value from /app/memory/test_credentials.md; a final re-login with the ORIGINAL password was verified. login_attempts collection was not touched (only one bad-password login attempt was performed).
context_for_next_testing_agent: All auth testids exist and behave correctly (login-email-input, login-password-input, login-submit-btn, login-error, user-menu-btn, user-menu-email, user-menu-change-password, user-menu-logout, change-password-dialog, pwd-current-input, pwd-new-input, pwd-confirm-input, pwd-error, pwd-submit-btn, auth-loading). Token key in localStorage = 'lt_token'. Report/photo URLs use ?token= via withToken() in api.js. Only outstanding issue is the 401 interceptor whitelist for /auth/change-password. When retesting the fix, replay: login → open change-password dialog → wrong current + valid new/confirm → expect pwd-error visible AND user still on the current page (no redirect to /login) AND lt_token unchanged.
rca_of_the_issue: Root cause: /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js lines 16-25 — the axios response interceptor treats every 401 as a session-invalid event and unconditionally clears the token + redirects to /login, only whitelisting the /auth/login endpoint. The change-password endpoint returns 401 on a wrong current_password (backend design confirmed by main agent self-test), so the interceptor kicks in, ChangePasswordDialog's own catch block never gets to setError(), the dialog unmounts, and the user is forcibly logged out. Fix: whitelist '/auth/change-password' (and, optionally, use a dedicated header/flag on requests that should not trigger the global logout).
